entry_points.name: delete_account
entry_points.note: HTTP route at gallery/<int:pk>/delete/ that calls delete() on the Account row.

entry_points.name: Account
entry_points.note: Account is registered in the Django admin, whose delete action removes the row.

stores.name: gallery_account

fields.name: joined_at
fields.note: Timestamp set when the account row is created.

erasure.note: The delete_account view calls account.delete(), which removes the row from gallery_account.

stores.note: Table holding one row per account holder.

stores.name: gallery_photo

fields.name: caption
fields.note: Free-text field a person types into; the schema does not constrain what it holds.

fields.name: taken_at
fields.note: Timestamp set when the photo row is created.

erasure.note: The foreign key to Account uses on_delete=models.CASCADE, so deleting the account row deletes the photo rows.

stores.note: Table holding photo rows, each pointing at one account.

stores.name: gallery_comment

fields.name: body
fields.note: Free-text field a person types into; the schema does not constrain what it holds.

fields.name: posted_at
fields.note: Timestamp set when the comment row is created.

erasure.note: The foreign key to Account uses on_delete=models.CASCADE, so deleting the account row deletes the comment rows.

stores.note: Table holding comment rows, each pointing at one account.

stores.name: photo.image

fields.name: image
fields.note: Uploaded image file stored under photo/images/; the schema does not constrain its content.

erasure.note: The only file-deleting receiver, delete_attached_image, is registered with sender=Comment, and Comment carries no image field, so deleting a Photo row leaves the uploaded file on disk.

stores.note: Files written by the ImageField on Photo, under the upload_to prefix photo/images/.
